correctness.rationale: Back forces each source maximum to map to a target maximum. A leaf's principal filter has two worlds, too few to lift the target center's filter when s≥2, so surjectivity forces center to center. Forth then permits exactly the matched leaf or the matched maximum at each source leaf. Each target leaf must be hit, and lifting there forces its target maximum to be hit by the corresponding source edge; hence the center's entire filter is lifted. This supplies both directions of the word bijection and the missing-letter inclusion–exclusion. The center is the unique minimum with multiple strict successors, so the automorphisms are exactly arm permutations. After source permutations only the tagged multiplicities at each index matter; target permutations make these pairs unordered. There are n types of total size n, as required by the product. In independent Python enumeration I tested equality of principal-filter images for all onto functions and counted orbits by explicit multiplication by arm permutations. For (r,s)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3),(4,2), the pairs (maps,orbits) were (2,1),(0,0),(18,2),(6,1),(110,6). The frozen replay paths are artifacts/verify_star.py and artifacts/verification_output.txt. The uploaded sweep at lines 78–81 actually samples only s≤r, so those sweep assertions alone do not test nonexistence. Universal correctness follows from the proof, not these finite checks.
